# Onramp

> Onramp is a developer onboarding platform. It indexes a team's GitHub repository into a live architecture map, generates a guided learning path and right-sized first issues from that map, answers new-hire questions with file-and-line citations from the real code, and shows engineering leads which new developers are ramping and which are stuck.

## Key Pages
- [Product overview](https://developer-onboard.vercel.app/): what Onramp does and how it works
- [Why Onramp](https://developer-onboard.vercel.app/why-onramp): comparison with general-purpose coding agents and wikis
- [Pricing](https://developer-onboard.vercel.app/pricing.md): plans, limits and prices (machine-readable)
- [Docs](https://developer-onboard.vercel.app/docs): getting started, connecting a repo, API
- [Blog](https://developer-onboard.vercel.app/blog): onboarding cost, time-to-first-PR, how the grounded mentor works
- [Security](https://developer-onboard.vercel.app/security): current controls, and what is not yet in place

## The problem Onramp solves
New engineers ramp by interrupting senior engineers. Institutional knowledge lives in seniors' heads and stale docs, so every hire re-asks the same questions, and engineering leads cannot see who is stuck until it shows up as missed delivery. Onramp makes the codebase answer first and makes the ramp visible.

## Core capabilities
- **Live architecture map**: a searchable dependency graph of the repository, rebuilt when the code changes
- **Ask (grounded repo Q&A)**: plain-English questions answered from the indexed code, with file-and-line citations and an import-graph check on the answer
- **Learning paths**: generated from the repository's own modules, with quizzes
- **First issues**: scoped starter tasks sized for a new hire's first week
- **Task and review queue**: assign, submit, review and approve onboarding tasks; merged PRs close the task
- **Ramp dashboard for leads**: ramp days against a team benchmark, stuck-developer alerts, senior-time cost, reviewer load
- **Knowledge map**: which people know which parts of the code, and where knowledge is concentrated in one person

## Who it is for
- Engineering managers, CTOs and VPs of Engineering at teams hiring developers regularly (roughly 5 to 200 engineers)
- Senior engineers who answer most of the new-hire questions
- New developers joining an unfamiliar codebase
- HR and people-ops teams running onboarding programs

## How it differs
- **Grounded in the team's repository**: answers cite real files; a generic coding assistant has no view of the team's onboarding state
- **Onboarding is a tracked workflow**: progress, gating, review and sign-off are recorded, not left in a wiki
- **Visibility for leads is a by-product**: ramp and stuck signals come from tasks people already do
- **Every feature on every plan**: plans differ by team size and volume, not by feature gates
- **Multi-provider AI routing**: no single model provider is load-bearing

## Languages
Repository indexing covers Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust and Java; other languages are indexed at file level.

## Pricing summary (INR, billed via Razorpay)
- **Free**: ₹0, 1 member, 1 repository, 50 AI credits per month
- **Startup**: ₹999/month or ₹9,999/year, up to 5 members, 10 repositories, 5,000 AI credits per month
- **Professional**: ₹2,999/month or ₹29,999/year, up to 20 members, 50 repositories, 50,000 AI credits per month, 14-day trial
- **Enterprise**: custom pricing, unlimited members, repositories and credits; SSO and SLA scoped per customer

## Status and honesty notes
- Onramp is early. There are no published customer case studies yet.
- Onramp is not SOC 2 certified. See the security page for the controls that are in place today.
